title: The Counter-Reading
openingText: Vask is taking readings off the observatory ring at an altitude where speaking costs something, and he does not stop while you approach. 'Somebody rotated this instrument off true, deliberately, with wedges,' he says, to the instrument. 'The interesting number is not the bearing. It is the size of the lie. Do you have anything, or are you just cold?'
dialogueWalkaway: Then take your observations elsewhere. I have three hours of light and no interest.
dialogueAccept: Agreed, and I will credit you in the record, which you may find is worth more than the coin.
confidence: Vask has provisioned for four days and intends to stay eleven.

clauses.text: Vask's working: what the ring pointed at before somebody wedged it, and when.
Your name in a Lantern Order record. Doors in the Sunken Archive open on it.
He teaches you to read ground the way he reads sky. It transfers better than it should.
You haul his brass down the mountain. It is heavy and he is not sorry.
Their survey of the district, annotated: the ground and what lies under it
Your field notes from the road
You carry their samples to the next waystone
Reading rights in your guild's library
